items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: I had a cassette of J.J. Johnson with Horace Silver and Woody Show and Joe Henderson in my — and I had a cassette player back then and I had that cassette.

ctx.x: That’s my phone but I’m going to let it ring. That chord I found in school when I was in college and that’s a C sharp 7 sharp 9 and that’s something that Horace Silver played. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

And I took it off and I was showing my friend one day. And Roger Pemberton, I’ve told this story before, but Roger Pemberton was giving us a two person arranging lesson. And He came in the door and I said, “Roger what’s this?” And I hit that chord and without thinking he said, “That’s a C sharp 7 sharp 9.” And that just blew my mind away. I said, “Well how can you tell?” And he said, “Well it just sounds like it.” And I silently moved it up to E 7 sharp 9 and hit it. And I said, “What if I hit that?” He said,…

items.title: Aebersold Jamey — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: There you’ve got Volume 6 with Charlie Parker, and then Miles Davis, Sonny Rollins and Woody Shaw.

Incidentally, the Volume 1, the Volume 3, the Volume 6... Volume 14—Benny Golson. Volume 17—Horace Silver. Volume 18—Horace Silver. We, as of the last year or two...we have slowed those records down, those Play-A-Longs, and now they have two CDs— slower tempos and original tempos. Because jazz education has moved through the years down and down age-wise, so you’ve got 10-, 11- and 12-, 13-year-old people trying to play Volume 1, our Charlie Parker tunes, our Horace Silver tunes. So we’ve been able to digitally…
And was it pitch control...not pitch control...
